# OS package dependencies for lkp-deps.sh
# =========================================
#
# This file is parsed by lkp-deps.sh, do not need to touch the script to add,
# remove, or rename a dependency.
#
# Format:
#   [canonical-name]
#   <package-manager>=<override>
#
# - Each dependency starts with its canonical name in [brackets]. The
#   canonical name follows RPM (dnf/yum/zypper) naming conventions, since
#   that is shared by most of the officially supported distros (CentOS,
#   Euler, Anolis, CloudOS, Rocky Linux, Oracle, Redhat).
# - A [canonical-name] block with no lines under it is installed under that
#   same name on every package manager (e.g. "git", "make").
# - Add an override line "<manager>=<name>" underneath a block to install a
#   different package name on that package manager. Supported managers:
#   apt, pacman, zypper, apk. (dnf/yum always use the canonical name.)
# - Use "<manager>=SKIP" when the dependency is already bundled with
#   another package on that distro (nothing extra needs installing).
# - Lines starting with # are comments and blank lines are ignored, so feel
#   free to leave notes next to tricky entries.
#
# Example - add a brand new dependency:
#   [some-new-lib-devel]
#   apt=libsome-new-dev
#   pacman=some-new-lib
#
# Note: "perf" is intentionally NOT listed here. Its package name is
# kernel-version-specific on Ubuntu/Debian (linux-tools-$(uname -r)), so it
# is installed by the dedicated install_perf() function in lkp-deps.sh
# instead of the generic resolver below.
